test_title: PYST 20: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In its advisory capacity, the Union Cabinet’s advice to the President of India is considered:

options.text: overruled by the Speaker of the Lower House

solution:
The correct answer is __**binding to the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Cabinet's advice to the President of India is **binding under Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The President is constitutionally obligated to act in accordance with the advice provided by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This principle emphasizes the concept of a parliamentary democracy where the President functions as a nominal head, while real executive power resides with the Council of Ministers.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 made it explicit that the President "shall act in accordance with such advice."
 
• Although the President may initially return advice for reconsideration, if the same advice is sent back, the President is bound to accept it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74(1):** This article states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, and the President shall act in accordance with such advice.
 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):** This amendment explicitly made the President's compliance with the advice of the Council of Ministers mandatory, strengthening the parliamentary system of governance.
 
• **Reconsideration Power:** While the President can send a recommendation back to the Council of Ministers for reconsideration, once the advice is reiterated, it becomes binding.
 
• **Nominal vs. Real Executive:** The President is the nominal executive head, while the Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, exercises real executive authority.
 
• **Parliamentary Democracy:** India follows a parliamentary system of governance where the President acts as the constitutional head, and the Council of Ministers is responsible to the Parliament.
